nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-01.title: Two right triangles
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-01.body:
At first the bottom is $\sqrt{25^2-20^2}=15$ ft from the wall. After slipping, the top is $7$ ft high and the bottom is $\sqrt{25^2-7^2}=24$ ft away. It moves $24-15=9$ ft.

**Answer: 9**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-02.title: Compare to the radius
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-02.body:
Let the small square have side $2x$, centered on the diameter. Its top corner is on the circle: $x^2+(2x)^2=R^2$, so its area is $4x^2=\frac45R^2$. The square inscribed in the circle has diagonal $2R$, so area $\frac12(2R)^2=2R^2$. The ratio of the areas is $\frac{4/5}{2}=\frac25$, so the large square has area $40\cdot\frac52=100$.

**Answer: 100**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-02.title: Find $R$ directly
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-02.body:
$4x^2=40$ gives $x^2=10$, so $R^2=5x^2=50$. The square inscribed in the circle has area $2R^2=100$.

**Answer: 100**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-03.title: Groups of 21
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-03.body:
$21$ apples cost \$7 and sell for \$9, a profit of \$2. For \$40 he needs $20$ such groups: $420$ apples.

**Answer: 420**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-03.title: Profit per apple
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-03.body:
Profit per apple is $\frac37-\frac13=\frac{2}{21}$ dollars, so he needs $40\div\frac{2}{21}=420$ apples.

**Answer: 420**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-05.title: Triangular numbers
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-05.body:
The last copy of $N$ is term $\frac{N(N+1)}{2}$. For $N=31$ that is term $496$, and for $N=32$ it is term $528$. So terms $497$ through $528$ are all $32$, including term $500$.

**Answer: 32**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-06.title: Man-days
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-06.body:
The job takes $xy$ man-days, so one man needs $xy$ days and $x+z$ men need $\frac{xy}{x+z}$ days.

**Answer: $\frac{xy}{x+z}$**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-07.title: Set up the sides
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-07.body:
Let the width be $x$ and the length $2x$. Then $P=6x$, $x=\frac P6$, and the area is $2x^2=\frac{2P^2}{36}=\frac{P^2}{18}$.

**Answer: $\frac{P^2}{18}$**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-08.title: Quadratic formula
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-08.body:
The roots are $\frac{-3\pm\sqrt{29}}{2}$, which differ by $\sqrt{29}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{29}$**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-09.title: Count pairs
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-09.body:
With $N$ people there are $\frac{N(N-1)}{2}$ handshakes. $N(N-1)=552=24\cdot23$, so $N=24$.

**Answer: 24**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-10.title: Law of Cosines
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-10.body:
Let $BC=x$, $AC=90-x$. Then $(90-x)^2=80^2+x^2-2\cdot80x\cos60^\circ$: $8100-180x=6400-80x$, so $x=17$. The sides are $80$, $17$, $73$; the shortest is $17$.

**Answer: 17**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-10.title: Altitude
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-10.body:
Drop altitude $CD$ to $AB$ and let $BD=m$. Then $BC=2m$, $CD=m\sqrt3$, $AD=80-m$, $AC=90-2m$. From $(90-2m)^2=3m^2+(80-m)^2$: $8100-360m=6400-160m$, so $m=\frac{17}{2}$ and $BC=17$.

**Answer: 17**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-11.title: Triangles and sectors
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-11.body:
Each chord of length $10$ forms an equilateral triangle with the center. The two chords are on opposite sides of the center (equal parallel chords on the same side would coincide). The region consists of the two equilateral triangles of side $10$ and two $120^\circ$ sectors of radius $10$: $2\cdot25\sqrt3+\frac23\cdot100\pi=50\sqrt3+\frac{200\pi}{3}$.

**Answer: $50\sqrt3+\frac{200\pi}{3}$**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-11.title: Subtract segments
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-11.body:
Each chord cuts off a segment of a $60^\circ$ sector: $\frac{100\pi}{6}-25\sqrt3$. The region is $100\pi-2\left(\frac{50\pi}{3}-25\sqrt3\right)=\frac{200\pi}{3}+50\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $50\sqrt3+\frac{200\pi}{3}$**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-12.title: Add lines one at a time
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-12.body:
One line makes $2$ regions. The $n$th line meets the previous $n-1$ lines at distinct points, so it passes through $n$ regions and splits each in two, adding $n$ regions. Total $2+2+3+\cdots+10=56$.

**Answer: 56**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-12.title: Formula
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-12.body:
$n$ lines in general position form $1+n+\binom n2$ regions: $1+10+45=56$.

**Answer: 56**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-13.title: Six equilateral triangles
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-13.body:
The hexagon has side $12$ and splits into $6$ equilateral triangles of area $\frac{144\sqrt3}{4}=36\sqrt3$. Total $216\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $216\sqrt3$**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-14.title: Reversed polynomial
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-14.body:
The reciprocals are roots of $-8x^2-5x+1=0$ (reverse the coefficients), whose root sum is $-\frac{-5}{-8}=-\frac58$.

**Answer: $-\frac58$**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-16.title: Track the water
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-16.body:
The $3.6$ ounces of non-acid must be $20\%$ of the final mix, so the mix is $18$ ounces and $6$ ounces of acid are added.

**Answer: 6**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-18.title: Solve for the leg
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-18.body:
With leg $x$, $2x+x\sqrt2=2$, so $x=\frac{2}{2+\sqrt2}=2-\sqrt2$. The area is $\frac12x^2=\frac12(6-4\sqrt2)=3-2\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $3-2\sqrt2$**

nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-18.title: Scale a standard triangle
nyciml-2009-10-spring-sophfrosh-18.body:
The $1$-$1$-$\sqrt2$ triangle has perimeter $2+\sqrt2$ and area $\frac12$. Scaling by $k=\frac{2}{2+\sqrt2}=2-\sqrt2$ multiplies the area by $k^2=6-4\sqrt2$, giving $3-2\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $3-2\sqrt2$**
